extracted.intended_audience: broadband internet service providers, IoT product manufacturers, Cybersecurity Label Administrators (CLAs), Cybersecurity Testing Laboratories (CyberLABs), Lead Administrator applicants, and FCC compliance/legal teams
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements (47 CFR Part 8) governing broadband transparency disclosures and a voluntary FCC IoT cybersecurity labeling program, including application, testing, accreditation, post-market surveillance, registry, and enforcement rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broadband transparency disclosure requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person providing broadband internet access service shall publicly disclose accurate information regarding the network management practices, performance characteristics, and commercial terms of its broadband internet access services sufficient to enable consumers to make informed choices regarding the purchase and use of such services and entrepreneurs and other small businesses to develop, market, and maintain internet offerings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such disclosure shall be made via a publicly available, easily accessible website or through transmittal to the Commission. The disclosure must be accurate and sufficient for consumer decision-making and for third-party development/market activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broadband consumer label creation and display
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person providing broadband internet access service shall create and display an accurate broadband consumer label for each stand-alone broadband internet access service it currently offers for purchase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The label must be prominently displayed, publicly available, and easily accessible to consumers, including consumers with disabilities, at the point of sale, with the content and in the format prescribed by the Commission (see 'Fixed or Mobile Broadband Consumer Disclosure' figure).

rubrics_metrics.name: Label display at each point of sale
rubrics_metrics.description: Broadband internet access service providers shall display the label required under paragraph (a)(1) of this section at each point of sale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Point of sale includes a provider's website and any alternate sales channels (provider-owned retail location, third-party retail location, over the phone). For provider websites, the label must be displayed in close proximity to the associated advertised service plan. Point of sale also includes the time a consumer begins investigating and comparing offerings at their location. For alternate channels, providers must document each instance when directing a consumer to a label and retain such documentation for two years OR establish and retain business practices/training materials for two years and provide upon Commission request within 30 days. For E-Rate and Rural Health Care programs, point of sale is when a provider submits its bid to a program participant. Providers offering online account portals must also make each customer's label easily accessible in such portals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Machine-readable labels and dedicated URL
rubrics_metrics.description: The content of the label must be displayed on the provider's website in a machine-readable format and providers must provide the information in any label separately in a spreadsheet file format via a dedicated URL that contains all of their labels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providers must publicize the URL with the label data in the required transparency disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Label language requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The label must be provided in English and in any other languages in which the broadband internet access service provider markets its services in the United States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Label archival retention
rubrics_metrics.description: Providers shall maintain an archive of all labels for a period of no less than two years from the time the service plan reflected in the label is no longer available for purchase by a new subscriber and the provider has removed the label from its website or alternate sales channels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providers must provide archived labels to the Commission upon request within thirty days and to an existing customer whose service plan is associated with the archived label within thirty days. Providers are not required to display a label once the associated service plan is no longer offered to new subscribers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Label enforcement and non-safe-harbor
rubrics_metrics.description: Broadband consumer label requirements and the transparency rule are subject to enforcement using the same processes and procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The label is not a safe harbor from the transparency rule or any other requirements established by the Commission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance deadlines and phased implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: Compliance with specified label and transparency provisions is required by set dates depending on provider size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providers with 100,000 or fewer subscriber lines: compliance with paragraphs (a)(1),(2),(4)-(6) required as of October 10, 2024. All other providers: required as of April 10, 2024, except the requirement to make labels accessible in online account portals is delayed for all providers until October 10, 2024. Compliance with machine-readable/spreadsheet URL requirement is required for all providers as of October 10, 2024.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of broadband internet access service (mass-market)
rubrics_metrics.description: Broadband internet access service is a mass-market retail service by wire or radio that provides the capability to transmit data to and receive data from all or substantially all internet endpoints, including incidental capabilities enabling operation of the communications service, but excluding dial-up access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The term includes functional equivalents and services used to evade protections; 'mass-market' excludes service offerings customized for the customer through individually negotiated agreements even if supported by federal universal service support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Network management reasonableness
rubrics_metrics.description: A network management practice is reasonable if it is appropriate and tailored to achieving a legitimate network management purpose, taking into account the particular network architecture and technology of the broadband internet access service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation by reference of standards for labeling program
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain ISO/IEC standards (e.g., ISO/IEC 17011:2017, ISO/IEC 17025:2017, ISO/IEC 17065:2012) are incorporated by reference and apply to the labeling program (accreditation bodies, testing labs, certifying bodies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These incorporated materials are available for inspection at the FCC and NARA and may impose specific accreditation/testing requirements referenced elsewhere in this subpart.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of the IoT labeling program
rubrics_metrics.description: The labeling program is established to elevate the Nation's cybersecurity posture and provide consumers with assurances regarding baseline cybersecurity, thereby addressing risks of harmful radiofrequency interference to and from consumer IoT products.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program is voluntary and allows a complying consumer IoT product to display an FCC IoT Label.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key definitions for labeling program
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions provided for terms used in the subpart, including 'affiliate', 'consumer IoT products', 'Cybersecurity Label Administrator (CLA)', 'CyberLAB', 'Cyber Trust Mark', 'FCC IoT Label', 'intentional radiator', 'internet-connected device', 'IoT device', 'IoT product', 'labeling program', 'Lead Administrator', 'product components', and 'registry'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions set substantive scope (e.g., consumer IoT products exclude FDA-regulated medical devices and motor vehicles; IoT device requires at least one transducer and at least one network interface; IoT product includes device plus necessary components such as backend/app). See detailed definitions in § 8.203.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on FCC IoT Label for products from listed sources
rubrics_metrics.description: All consumer IoT products produced by sources listed in this subpart are prohibited from obtaining use of the FCC IoT Label.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes: communications equipment on the Covered List pursuant to 47 CFR 1.50002; IoT products containing devices/components produced by entities on specified lists; products produced by entities or affiliates on the Covered List; products produced by entities on the Dept. of Commerce Entity List or DoD 'Chinese Military Companies' list; products produced by entities suspended or debarred from federal procurements (e.g., SAM ineligible).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cybersecurity labeling authorization scope and attachment
rubrics_metrics.description: A cybersecurity labeling authorization is issued by a CLA under Commission authority to grant an applicant permission to display the FCC IoT Label on packaging for a complying consumer product based on compliance with program requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorization attaches to all units of the complying product subsequently marketed that are identical to the sample determined to comply, except for permissive changes or other variations authorized by the Commission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'identical' for authorization
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'identical' means identical within the variation that can be expected to arise as a result of quantity production techniques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsible party for continued compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant to whom the cybersecurity labeling authorization is issued is responsible for continued compliance with the program requirements for continued use of the FCC IoT Label.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application form, content, and certification requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications must be submitted in writing to a CLA in the form and format prescribed by the Commission and accompanied by all information required by the subpart; applicants must provide all information the CLA requires to determine compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical test data must be signed by the person who performed or supervised the tests and attested accurate. The CLA may require qualifications for the signer. 'Signed' may be original handwritten or electronic symbol intended as signature. Applications and related statements must be signed by applicant or authorized agent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant declarations under penalty of perjury
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must declare under penalty of perjury that specified statements are true and correct, including that the product meets program requirements; applicant is not on the Covered List; product does not include 'covered' equipment; product not produced by entities on certain prohibited lists; product not owned/controlled by suspended/debarred entities; applicant has taken every reasonable measure to create a securable product; applicant will diligently identify critical vulnerabilities and promptly issue software updates until the disclosed support period end date unless not reasonably needed; applicant will not disclaim or attempt to limit enforceability of declarations or label-related representations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If listed sources change after the declaration but before grant, the applicant must provide a new declaration. Applicant must designate a U.S.-located agent for service of process (attested by agent signature if different). U.S. applicants may self-designate as agent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of minimum support period and update commitments
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant must disclose the support period end date in the registry and declare they will diligently identify critical vulnerabilities and promptly issue software updates correcting them until that disclosed support end date, unless not reasonably needed to protect against security failures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternatively, the applicant may state the device is unsupported and purchasers should not rely on manufacturer to release updates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant conditions and documentation of grants
rubrics_metrics.description: A CLA will grant authorization if it finds from examination of the application and supporting data that the product complies with program requirements; grants will be made in writing showing the effective date and identifying the CLA and the Commission as the issuing authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cybersecurity certification does not attach until the application has been granted. In disputes, the Commission is final arbiter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application dismissal grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: An application not in accordance with the provisions of this subpart may be dismissed; applicant may request dismissal prior to determination; failure to submit requested material within time may result in dismissal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application denial and notice
rubrics_metrics.description: If the CLA cannot make the required findings of compliance, it will deny the application and notify the applicant including a statement of reasons for the denial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review procedures for CLA decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Any party aggrieved by a CLA action must first seek review from the CLA; after that, may seek review from the Commission. Requests for review to CLA or Commission must be filed within 60 days of CLA decision; parties must adhere to time periods in 47 CFR 1.45 for oppositions/replies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public Safety and Homeland Security Bureau (PSHSB) will consider requests for review; novel questions go to full Commission. Standard of review: PSHSB conducts de novo review of CLA decisions; Commission conducts de novo review for novel questions of fact, law, or policy (except it will not conduct de novo review of Bureau decisions issued under delegated authority). Time periods: PSHSB shall act within 45 days (may extend up to 90 days); Commission shall issue written decision within 45 days for novel matters (extensions allowed). While seeking review, party is not authorized to use the FCC IoT Label until Commission issues final decision authorizing use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on grants and marketing restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: A grant remains effective until set aside, revoked, withdrawn, rescinded, surrendered, or a termination date established; no person shall use or reference the FCC IoT Label or Cyber Trust Mark in a deceptive or misleading manner in advertising or materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complaint, defect, and design-change reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: When a complaint is filed with the Commission (directly or via Lead Administrator/other party) concerning a product's non-compliance, and the Commission determines the complaint justified, the Commission may require the grantee to investigate and report results within 20 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report shall indicate actions taken or proposed to correct the defect in future production and with reference to articles in possession of users, sellers, and distributors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record retention for grantees
rubrics_metrics.description: Grantee shall maintain records of original design/specifications and changes that may affect compliance; records of production inspection/testing procedures; records of test results demonstrating compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Records retained for two years after marketing of associated product permanently discontinued, or until conclusion of an investigation or proceeding if grantee is notified of such an action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Termination of authorization (automatic termination grounds)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorization is automatically terminable by Bureau notice if: (1) false statements/representations in application/materials/records required to be kept; (2) subsequent inspection/operation shows product does not conform to technical requirements or original representations; (3) conditions arise that would have warranted refusing authorization; (4) grantee or affiliate has been listed as prohibited per § 8.204.

rubrics_metrics.name: CyberLAB accreditation and competence requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A CyberLAB providing testing for products seeking authorization must be accredited by a recognized accreditation body, which must attest the CyberLAB has demonstrated technical expertise in cybersecurity testing/conformity assessment of IoT devices; compliance with ISO/IEC 17025; knowledge of FCC rules/procedures; necessary equipment/facilities/personnel; documented conformity assessment procedures; implementation of controls to eliminate potential conflicts of interest; that the CyberLAB is not an entity identified by listed sources of prohibition; and that it has certified truth/accuracy of all submitted information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once accredited the CyberLAB will be periodically audited/reassessed; Lead Administrator will verify not being listed in prohibited lists; Lead Administrator will maintain and publish list of accredited CyberLABs (inclusion not FCC endorsement). Laboratories with scope covering required measurements and accredited by a PSHSB-recognized organization based on ISO/IEC 17025 will be deemed competent. Reassessment intervals not to exceed two years and must comply with accreditor requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition criteria for CyberLAB accreditation bodies
rubrics_metrics.description: A party seeking recognition as a laboratory accreditation body by PSHSB must submit a written request and demonstrate credentials, including successful completion of an ISO/IEC 17011 peer review (e.g., signatory to acceptable accreditation agreement), experience accrediting conformity assessment testing labs to ISO/IEC 17025, accreditation personnel/assessors with technical experience on FCC cybersecurity rules, and procedures/policies for accrediting testing labs for FCC cybersecurity certification programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PSHSB may request additional information as needed to determine credentials and qualifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: CLA approval, eligibility, and accreditation requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: To be approved/recognized as a CLA, an entity must meet requirements in the section (including accreditation under ISO/IEC 17065 where applicable), demonstrate technical expertise, impartiality, controls for conflicts of interest, not be owned/controlled/affiliated with entities on prohibited lists, and have competence to evaluate products per Commission rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission may conditionally approve CLAs provided they commit to obtain ISO/IEC 17065 accreditation within six months, and must demonstrate controls to eliminate conflicts of interest and impartiality (e.g., avoiding preferential treatment, 'application line jumping', or heightened scrutiny of non-aligned entities). CLAs shall not outsource review/decision activities (they may outsource evaluation/testing but retain responsibility and oversight per ISO/IEC 17065). Commission will not approve organizations listed in § 8.204. Commission may withdraw approval for cause or if accreditation withdrawn; withdrawal notice and opportunity to respond provided. A published list of recognized CLAs will be maintained.

rubrics_metrics.name: CLA scope of responsibilities and prohibitions
rubrics_metrics.description: A CLA shall receive/evaluate applications and supporting data, grant authorization in accordance with Commission rules, accept test data from Lead Administrator-recognized CyberLABs (and not unnecessarily repeat tests), may establish and assess fees, dismiss improper applications, ensure manufacturers provide required registry information, participate in consumer education with Lead Administrator, receive complaints about labeled products and refer to Lead Administrator/PSHSB, and share Lead Administrator expenses as required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A CLA may not make policy, interpret statute/rules, grant waivers of the subpart rules, or take enforcement actions. All CLA actions are subject to Commission review. CLAs must maintain confidentiality of non-public information and implement administrative/technical/procedural/physical safeguards to protect confidentiality and prevent unauthorized disclosure/use.

rubrics_metrics.name: CLA post-market surveillance obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: In accordance with ISO/IEC 17065, CLAs shall perform appropriate post-market surveillance activities based on type testing of a certain number of samples of product types for which the CLA has certified use of the Label.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PSHSB may request grantee submit product samples directly to the evaluating CLA for post-market surveillance; such tests count toward minimum sample testing requirements. If CLA determines product fails to comply, it shall immediately notify grantee and Commission in writing; grantee must provide a report on corrective actions and CLA shall report to Commission within 30 days. CLAs must submit periodic reports of post-market surveillance activities and findings in formats/dates specified by the Commission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead Administrator duties and operational requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If multiple CLAs are selected, the Commission will select a Lead Administrator to interface with the Commission on behalf of CLAs, coordinate CLAs and stakeholder meetings, accept/review/approve/deny lab recognition requests, maintain lists of recognized labs, and perform additional administrative responsibilities for the labeling program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Within 90 days of election, Lead Administrator must collaborate with CLAs/stakeholders to submit recommendations to the Bureau identifying/developing technical standards/testing procedures for at least one class of IoT products; recommend renewal frequencies for product authority; recommend procedures for post-market surveillance; recommend registry updates (including additional languages) and label design/placement details (including whether to include support end date); within 45 days of NIST guideline updates recommend modifications to stay aligned; submit reports on CLAs' post-market surveillance; develop and participate in consumer education campaign; receive/coordinate resolution of registry technical problems; facilitate CLA coordination; create/implement cybersecurity risk management plan available to Commission upon request; submit forward-looking cost estimates and audited annual financial statements; implement internal controls to prevent improper payments and fraud; and maintain adequate operations to perform duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for designation as Lead Administrator
rubrics_metrics.description: Entities seeking designation must submit how they will execute duties and demonstrate previous IoT cybersecurity experience, prior role in IoT labeling (if any), capacity to execute duties, stakeholder engagement plans to develop Bureau recommendations, a proposed consumer education campaign, and any additional information supporting selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: IoT Registry content and API requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A grantee authorized to use the FCC IoT Label shall provide product information to the public via a dynamic, decentralized, publicly accessible registry through a common API that is secure by design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required published information via the API includes: Product Name; Manufacturer name; Date product received authorization and current status; Name/contact of CLA that authorized the label; Name of lab that conducted conformity testing; Instructions on how to change default password (or state if cannot be changed); Information/link on how to configure device securely; Whether updates/patches are automatic and how to access them if not; The date until which the entity promises to diligently identify critical vulnerabilities and promptly issue updates (minimum support period) or a statement device is unsupported; Disclosure of whether manufacturer maintains a Hardware Bill of Materials (HBOM) and/or Software Bill of Materials (SBOM); and any additional data elements the Bureau deems necessary.
